subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lead-in: traffic congestion; the cartoon; a letter to a council director
outcomes: Talk about the feelings and effects of traffic congestion
Read a letter of complaint and answer questions about it

tf.s: A traffic jam happens when too many vehicles are crowded together and can't move.
tf.why: That is the meaning of a traffic jam.

tf.s: Drivers stuck in traffic often feel frustrated, angry or stressed.
tf.why: Waiting in traffic makes people tense.

tf.s: Congestion lowers the risk of road rage because drivers relax.
tf.why: Congestion makes drivers frustrated and impatient, so road rage increases.

tf.s: A congestion charge, park and ride, and car-share schemes are ways to reduce congestion.
tf.why: They all cut the number of cars in busy areas.

tf.s: Miss Smith worries that her boss will fire her because she is late.
tf.why: Traffic makes her late for work, so she feels stressed.

tf.s: Getting up earlier has completely solved Miss Smith's problem.
tf.why: It hasn't worked, because other people get up earlier too.

tf.s: Pollution is one of the problems caused by traffic congestion.
tf.why: Many cars waiting in traffic produce pollution.

tf.s: Car-sharing means every person drives their own car to work.
tf.why: Car-sharing means people travel together in one car.

tf.s: 'Beat the traffic' means to drive into other cars.
tf.why: It means travelling early to avoid the heavy traffic.

tf.s: Congestion has no effect on businesses.
tf.why: Businesses are affected when customers and workers are delayed.

o: Vehicles crowded and unable to move
boxes.why: In a traffic jam, cars can't move.

boxes.q: Why hasn't getting up earlier worked?
boxes.why: Everyone tries to beat the traffic.

o: Park outside town, take a bus in
boxes.why: It keeps cars out of the city centre.

o: Money paid to drive in busy areas
boxes.why: Paying to drive in makes some people leave the car.

boxes.q: Which is a problem caused by congestion?
boxes.why: Many waiting cars pollute the air.
You leave before the roads get busy.

boxes.why: She complains to a council director.

mcq.q: Which feelings do drivers stuck in traffic have?
Which list gives ways to reduce congestion?
o: Car-share, street closures, congestion charge, park and ride
More cars, more parking, cheaper fuel
mcq.why: These solutions reduce the number of cars.

mcq.q: What has Miss Smith done to solve her problem?
o: She has been getting up earlier, but it hasn't worked
She has bought a new car
She has moved to another city
mcq.why: Others get up early too, so the roads are still busy.

mcq.q: Which list shows problems caused by congestion?
o: Stress, road rage, pollution and businesses affected
mcq.why: These are the problems listed in the lesson.

mcq.q: Four colleagues live near each other and work in the same office. Which solution suits them?
mcq.why: Sharing one car means three fewer cars on the road.

mcq.q: A city wants to keep cars out of its centre but still let people come in. Which idea fits best?
o: Build more car parks in the centre
Make driving in the centre free
mcq.why: Drivers park outside and take a bus into the centre.

mcq.q: Ahmed leaves home at 5.30 a.m. to avoid busy roads. What is he trying to do?
mcq.why: Leaving very early helps you avoid the traffic.

mcq.q: Why does congestion increase the risk of road rage?
o: Drivers become frustrated, angry and impatient
mcq.why: Long waits make some drivers lose their temper.

mcq.q: Why does Miss Smith feel stressed?
o: She is late because of traffic and worries her boss will fire her
Her boss has given her a prize
mcq.why: Fear of losing her job adds to the stress of traffic.

mcq.q: Why might a congestion charge reduce traffic?
o: Some drivers choose other transport to avoid paying
mcq.why: A cost encourages people to share cars or use buses.
